title: Leading vs Open-Ended Question Sorter
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Entrepreneurship
description: A six-card sorting quiz in which learners classify discovery-interview questions about a mobile dog-grooming idea as open-ended or leading, with immediate green or amber feedback, a one-sentence explanation for each card, and an open-ended rewrite of every leading question.

prerequisites: Chapter 9: Discovery Interviews & the Reality Check
learningObjectives: Classify discovery-interview questions as open-ended or leading by applying the chapter's unbiased interview design principles

controls.label: Open-Ended
controls.purpose: Classify the current question as one that lets the customer supply the content

controls.label: Leading
controls.purpose: Classify the current question as one that suggests its own answer

controls.label: Try Again
controls.purpose: Reshuffle the cards and start over

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Classification quiz with immediate corrective feedback and worked rewrites
keyQuestions: Who supplies the content: the customer or the question?
Could a stranger answer "no" to this question without feeling awkward?
commonMisconceptions: Any question that mentions a problem is leading
A statement with "right?" at the end is a genuine question
assessmentOpportunities: Score at least 5 of 6 on a second, shuffled attempt
Rewrite a leading question from your own interview script as an open-ended question
